newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: INSTANT VIEW - S.Africa's 1997/98 budget.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - S.Africa's 1997/98 budget.

text.p: South African Finance Minister Trevor Manuel presented his 1997/98 (April-March) budget to parliament on Wednesday, pledging to cut the deficit to 4.0 percent of GDP from 5.1 percent this year, while also announcing plans to further relax exchange controls.
The following are reactions from analysts:
CONSTANTIN VAYENAS, UBS, LONDON

"The announcement that individuals will be able to hold foreign currency accounts is an extremely positive development. It reinforces the whole story of a prudent macro environment, otherwise individuals are going to start selling rand and buying dollrs.
"The rest of the budget, in terms of its targets, is broadly in line with what was expected."
PETER WORTHINGTON, JP MORGAN, LONDON

"It's a pretty positive budget overall with no big surprises on the fiscal front. I was a little disappointed that there hadn't been more privatisation proceeds...but on the exchange control front I believe they've done a good job with fairly comprehensive packages and relaxations which are not going lead to a huge outflow of currency tomorrow, but which should give a lot of confidence to corporates, financial institutions and individuals.
"Maybe we saw a more broad-based and visionary relaxation of exchange controls than people had anticipated."
DAWIE ROODT, EQUISEC, JOHANNESBURG
"The initial reaction on the market will be positive but it will be difficult to stick to the figures. A worrying factor is the decrease in capital expenditure."
HANIA FARHAN, ING BARINGS, JOHANNESBURG
"It looks like a very good budget, very strict on expansion of expenditure...so I would say it's a very prudent budget.

"On the exchange control front it looks pretty good for individuals -- which was expected -- but on institutional assets allowed out they didn't say much. The problem there, is that the pent-up demand from the institutions to take money out of the country is still going to be there.
"But the main thrust is that they are really going to be very strict on expenditure."
HENRY FLINT, MATHISON AND HOLLIDGE, JOHANNESBURG
"I think the moves on exchange controls are long overdue, but are very positive. It is what everyone has been looking for.
"I think the move to allow local residents to hold foreign currency accounts is very positive. Broadening the asset swap mechanism is also very positive.
"I think from now on we can expect exchange controls to be removed more rapidly."
KEVIN LINGS, NEDCOR, JOHANNESBURG

"My initial reaction is favourable. There are a number of encouraging features to it, particularly foreign exchange control relaxation, although some of the amounts are not quite clear so there is a sense of having to wait for that detail to get greater clarity."
"In terms of the GEAR announcement, the budget deficit puts it immediately in line with the targets set out within the GEAR document.
"Overall it is a significant step in the right direction."
HERMAN VAN PAPENDORP, SMK SECURITIES, JOHANNESBURG

"It (the budget) seems to me quite reasonable -- in line with market expectations -- but the one thing I'm worried about is the expenditure figure which is seen rising only 6.1 percent which to me seems a very optimistic scenario.

"That is the one worrying aspect...otherwise it is pretty close to figures anticipated. The income numbers are very conservative, which is fine, and on exchange controls there was nothing earth shattering but we're moving along and that is positive."
ERIC WOOD, INVESTEC MERCHANT BANK, JOHANNESBURG
"The bond market initially took it to be very bullish, but there was a little disappointment about the fact that there was no change in pension fund taxation.
"We were expecting a change in the tax on income to a tax on total assets, which would shift the current preference towards investment in equities.

"The second thing that has not come through, which may not have too many implications, was that we were expecting the scrapping of the asset swap mechanism and it to be replaced by a an allowance on the part of the local institutions to invest a percentage of their total assets.

"For the rest of it the budget is very good, expenditure down in real terms, the total borrowing requirement is towards the lower end of our expectations and should not put any pressure on the market."
SANDRA GORDON, SYFRETS, CAPE TOWN
"He has managed to balance the need for increeased spending on social delivery with the need to stick to macroeconomic targets.
"I like the fact that he was quite bold in terms of exchange control moves. They are finally seizing the opportunity and I think he may have marginally exceeded market expectations on that front."
-- Parliamentary newsroom -27-12-403-2502
